interpretation_guide: Instruction KV helps more than random additions: the designated general guidance is useful beyond adding the same amount of cache. Instruction text also recovers performance: clearer receiver instructions may provide the simpler repair. A learned interface would need a stronger justification. Instruction KV helps, but instruction text does not: the cached instruction representations merit further investigation; this would not by itself prove a unique mechanism. Random additions perform similarly: recovery is not specific to the instruction block. Neither instruction version helps enough: proceed to the calculation-block comparison. These are exploratory development comparisons. Adding context changes message length and attention, so improvement over R alone does not establish that instruction content matters. Equal-size random comparisons address that. The text-instruction condition is a practical alternative; it does not hold every computation identical.
